stageMeta.title: Operable Harness
headerComment: # Stage 10 — Operable Harness
# L10 = L9 + Operability.  Every plugin from Stage 09 is still here —
# the sandboxed, approval-gated, persistent agent with the L7 stateful-task
# closure (todo / plan-mode / goal / workspace), the L8 multi-agent closure
# (subagent registry + providers + jobs), and the L9 long-task runtime
# (workflow engine / ralph / token-meter / compaction) — plus the L10
# operability closure:
#   dsh-llm-retry          transient provider failures heal themselves:
#                          hooks the loop's agent/request-error waterfall,
#                          backs off (500ms→10s + jitter, 2 retries in the
#                          default "normal" mode) and appends durable
#                          llm/retry + llm/retry-started session events.
#                          No config of its own — per-provider policy lives
#                          in the adapter's optional `retryPolicy` key;
#                          omission = normal mode, so mounting alone turns
#                          retry on.
#   dsh-invariants         ctx.invariants registry: runtime assertions over
#                          the durable session log.  The registry alone
#                          installs no checks — each package may publish a
#                          `<pkg>/invariant` companion (inject:
#                          ["invariants"]) that registers its own checks.
#   dsh-session-telemetry  telemetry seam — still DISABLED, see below.
#   dsh-session-projection ctx.sessionProjections registry — mounted here,
#                          in L10, because its first consumer in this
#                          composition is session-stats.
#   dsh-session-stats      registers the `sessionStats` projection unit
#                          (turn/step counts, llm/tool/ttft/decode wall
#                          times).  ACTIVE at this level: its
#                          `sessionProjections` inject is now satisfied by
#                          dsh-session-projection above.
# The architectural concept: "runs" ≠ "operable".
#   retry      → transient faults self-heal       (the run survives)
#   telemetry  → session records can be exported   (the run is observable)
#   stats      → whole-session figures are folded  (the run is measurable)
#   invariants → runtime assertions over the log   (the run is audited)
# What --trace shows at this level that L9 did not: on a flaky gateway the
# trace gains `llm/retry` / `llm/retry-started` events around the same
# turn/step machinery (the smoke run's dead baseURL classifies as
# TRANSPORT, so retry fires twice before the error surfaces), and the
# session-projection registry now folds live `sessionStats` figures as
# those events stream by.
# Remaining gaps in the pinned 0.1.0-rc.6 dependency set (entries kept
# visible in inspect/diff, mounted `disabled`):
#   - dsh-session-telemetry is a pure Service Definition: its module
#     exports only the abstract SessionTelemetryBackend + coordinator and
#     NO plugin entry, so cordis rejects it as "invalid plugin".  A
#     backend implementation (e.g. an OTel package) is not installed.
#   - dsh-jobs, dsh-compaction and dsh-workflow are abstract Service
#     Definitions.  dsh-jobs throws by design when mounted directly;
#     dsh-compaction / dsh-workflow would double-register ctx.compaction /
#     ctx.workflowEngine next to their concrete providers
#     (dsh-compaction-basic, dsh-workflow-worker-thread).  Exactly one
#     implementation per context — the providers carry the runtime.
# The persona is frozen (byte-for-byte identical to L4/L5/L6) so the
# whole L4→L10 progression remains a single-variable experiment.
# Second L10 closure — retrieval + guard policies:
#   dsh-session-query    DISABLED (abstract seam; sqlite backend provides it)
#   dsh-session-query-sqlite  FTS5 session-history search — a retrieval
#                        capability, NOT a persistence backend
#   dsh-session-reference  cross-session snapshot references (untrusted ctx)
#   dsh-repeat-tool-reminder  advisory loop-breaker at 3/5/8 identical calls
#   dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy  enforces ToolDefinition.timeoutMs budgets
#   dsh-time-context     durable per-step timestamp + elapsed-time injection
stageMeta.driverQuestion: Fix the divide-by-zero bug in src/calculator.js and run the tests.

entry.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-sqlite
entry.configYaml:
config:
    # Required string.  Lives inside the disposable tmp workspace next to
    # ./sessions; missing directories are created owner-only by the plugin.
    path: ./storage/domain.db

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry
comments: # No config — the executor's schema is empty; policy lives in each
# provider profile's optional `retryPolicy` key (omitted above =
# "normal" mode: 2 retries on EMPTY_RESPONSE/RATE_LIMIT/SERVER/TIMEOUT/
# TRANSPORT, bounded 500ms→10s backoff + 10% jitter).  Hooks the loop's
# agent/request-error waterfall and appends durable llm/retry +
# llm/retry-started events — watch for them in --trace.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants
comments: # No config — defaults: enabled: true, empty allow/blocklists (every
# companion selected).  The registry alone installs NO checks; concrete
# runtime assertions come from per-package companions mountable as
# '@deepseek-ai/<pkg>/invariant' (not added here — the declared L10
# closure is the registry seam itself).

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-telemetry
comments: # DISABLED — still not a mountable plugin: the module exports only the
# abstract SessionTelemetryBackend class + SessionTelemetryCoordinator
# (no apply, no default plugin), so cordis rejects it as
# "invalid plugin".  The seam needs a backend implementation (e.g. an
# OTel package) that is not installed.  Entry kept for closure
# visibility in inspect/diff.
# Session projection registry (ctx.sessionProjections): folds per-session
# projection units from the durable log and serves them to consumers.
# Mounted in L10 because its first consumer in this composition is
# session-stats below; several earlier plugins (todo, plan-mode,
# token-meter, subagent) also register their units here now that the
# registry exists.

entries.name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection
comments: # ACTIVE at this level: the `sessionProjections` inject is satisfied
# above, so the `sessionStats` unit (turns, steps, llmMs, ttftMs,
# decodeMs, toolMs folded from the whole log) actually registers and
# folds live.  No config.
